checklist.step: Rebuild the covered-asset base for the price fluctuation reserve
actions: Export from Aladdin the month-end position file for the Japan general account: domestic equities, domestic bonds, foreign-currency bonds and equities, money-held-in-trust and real estate held for investment.
Map each position to the Art. 115 reserve category set by the Ordinance for Enforcement (equities, bonds, foreign-currency denominated assets, real estate) and drop categories the ordinance excludes.
Reconcile the position book values line by line to the SAP S/4HANA investment sub-ledger and clear any difference above JPY 1 million with the Controller before releasing the file.
Hand the signed covered-asset base to the Capital Management Manager with the reconciliation attached.
checklist.done: the covered-asset base ties to the investment sub-ledger and every Art. 115 category is populated with book values.

checklist.step: Compute the price fluctuation reserve accrual at the ordinance rates
actions: In the Art. 115 reserve worksheet enter the covered book value per category and apply the accumulation rate set by the Ordinance for Enforcement (domestic equities the highest band, domestic bonds the lowest, foreign-currency assets in between).
Compare the accumulated balance to the ordinance ceiling for each category and cap the accrual where the ceiling is already reached.
Compute the required accrual for the business year as (target balance − opening balance) and split it across the interim (30 September) and year-end (31 March) postings.
Send the worksheet to the Appointed Actuary and the Controller for concurrence before any journal is raised.
checklist.done: the accrual is computed per category at the ordinance rate, capped at the ceiling, and concurred by the Appointed Actuary and Controller.

checklist.step: Test whether any reserve drawdown is actually permitted
actions: Pull realised gains and losses on Art. 115 covered assets for the period from the GL disposal accounts.
Net the realised losses against realised gains inside each covered category and compare the net loss to the drawdown threshold prescribed by the FSA ordinance.
Where the net loss exceeds the threshold, compute the permitted drawdown as the excess only — never the whole loss — and document the arithmetic on the reserve worksheet.
Where the threshold is not breached, record 'no drawdown permitted' with the tested figures rather than leaving the line blank.
Route any proposed drawdown to the CFO for written approval before posting.
checklist.done: any drawdown is supported by a tested net realised loss above the prescribed threshold and carries written CFO approval.

checklist.step: Recalculate the solvency margin ratio for the month
actions: Load the month-end asset file, the Art. 116 policy reserve balance and the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve into the solvency margin model.

Build the numerator: capital and surplus, price fluctuation reserve, contingency reserve, general allowance for doubtful accounts, net unrealised gains on securities at the prescribed inclusion rate, and subordinated debt within its limit.

Build the denominator risk components — insurance risk, assumed interest rate risk, minimum guarantee risk on variable annuities, asset management risk and business management risk — and combine them with the prescribed correlation formula.
Compute SMR = numerator ÷ (0.5 × total risk) × 100 and record the result to one decimal place.
Attach the model run id and input hash so the number can be reproduced.
checklist.done: a reproducible SMR figure exists for the month with numerator, denominator and model run id recorded.

checklist.step: Recalculate the economic value-based solvency ratio alongside the statutory ratio
actions: Run the ESR model on the month-end economic scenario set using the FSA-prescribed ultimate forward rate and last liquid point for the JPY curve.
Compute eligible own funds as market-consistent assets less best-estimate liabilities less risk margin, then divide by the required capital at the 99.5% one-year confidence level.
Compare the ESR to the statutory SMR and explain any divergence above 20 percentage points in the commentary — interest rate duration mismatch is the usual driver.
Send the ESR pack to the Chief Risk Officer with the SMR result so both ratios are reviewed together.
checklist.done: ESR and SMR are produced from the same month-end data with a written explanation of the divergence.

checklist.step: Score both ratios against the intervention ladder
actions: Enter the month's SMR and ESR into the capital trigger register.
Score SMR against the ladder: above 300% green, 250–300% amber watch, 200–250% amber action, below 200% Category 1 prompt corrective action, below 100% Category 2, below 0% Category 3.
Score ESR against the 100% regulatory floor and the internal 130% risk appetite trigger.
Where the score changed from last month, set the register status and name the accountable executive on the row.
checklist.done: both ratios carry a dated trigger score and any change of status names an accountable executive.

checklist.step: Escalate an amber or red trigger inside one business day
actions: On any amber or red score, issue the trigger notification to the CFO, CEO and the Chair of the Risk Committee within one business day of the ratio being produced.
State in the notification the ratio, the driver (equity fall, JGB yield move, yen strength, reserve strengthening), the distance to the next threshold and the date of the next recalculation.
Call an out-of-cycle Risk Committee where the SMR is below 250% or the ESR below 110%.
Log the notification time against the ratio production time in the trigger register so the one-business-day rule is provable.
checklist.done: every amber/red score has a timestamped notification to CFO, CEO and Risk Committee Chair within one business day.

checklist.step: Build the management action menu before it is needed
actions: Maintain a costed menu of capital actions: equity hedging or de-risking of the price-variable portfolio, reinsurance of the variable annuity minimum guarantee block, subordinated debt issue, dividend suspension, and new-business volume throttling.
For each action record the SMR and ESR uplift in percentage points, the lead time in weeks and the approval body required.
Refresh the uplift estimates each quarter using the current balance sheet, not the estimate from launch.
Present the menu to the Risk Committee with the quarterly capital pack.
checklist.done: a costed, lead-timed action menu with current uplift estimates is tabled at the Risk Committee each quarter.

checklist.step: Draft the improvement plan the moment a Category 1 threshold is crossed
actions: On an SMR below 200%, open the improvement plan template within 5 business days of detection.
Set out the cause, the projected ratio path over the next 4 quarters, the selected management actions with dates, and the responsible executive per action.
Have the Appointed Actuary confirm the projected policy reserve and minimum guarantee assumptions used in the path.
Table the draft at the Board and record the resolution before any version is shared outside the company.
checklist.done: a Board-resolved improvement plan with a quarterly ratio path exists within 5 business days of a sub-200% reading.

checklist.step: Feed the ratio and the reserve position into the Board pack
actions: Publish to the board portal the monthly capital dashboard: SMR, ESR, price fluctuation reserve balance and headroom to ceiling, contingency reserve balance and trigger status.
Include the 24-month trend chart and the distance to the 200% Category 1 line in percentage points.
Record in the minutes that the Board received the capital position, naming the meeting date and the papers tabled.
Retain the pack and the minute extract as the governance evidence for the period.
checklist.done: each Board meeting minute records receipt of the capital dashboard, with the pack retained on the portal.

checklist.step: Reconcile the monitoring numbers to the statutory ledger before period close
actions: Tie the price fluctuation reserve balance in the monitoring pack to the statutory balance sheet reserve account at 30 September and 31 March.
Tie the policy reserve and outstanding claims reserve inputs to the Appointed Actuary's signed valuation summary.
Investigate and clear any difference before the close is locked; a monitoring number that never touched the ledger is treated as unsupported.
Sign the reconciliation and file it with the close binder.
checklist.done: monitoring reserve balances agree to the closed statutory ledger with a signed reconciliation on file.

checklist.step: Re-read the ordinance rates and formula each time the FSA moves them
actions: Subscribe the regulatory change inbox to FSA notifications and Cabinet Office Ordinance amendments touching Insurance Business Act Arts. 115, 116, 117 and 130.
On each amendment, record the amended accumulation rate, ceiling or risk factor, its effective date, and which model or worksheet must change.
Open a change request against the solvency margin model and the reserve worksheet with the effective date as the deadline.
Confirm with the Capital Model Actuary that the changed factor is live before the first affected period end.
checklist.done: every ordinance change has a logged effective date and a model/worksheet change confirmed live before the affected period end.

checklist.step: Prove the monitoring controls to the Appointed Actuary
actions: Review the capital monitoring packs for the year alongside the reserve adequacy work supporting the Art. 121 actuarial opinion.
Confirm the price fluctuation and contingency reserve balances used in the monitoring agree with the balances underlying the opinion.
Challenge any month where the SMR moved more than 30 percentage points without an explained driver.
Record the review and any qualification in the actuarial working papers.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary has reviewed the year's monitoring against the reserve basis and recorded any qualification.

checklist.step: Close out each trigger event with proof the ratio recovered
actions: For every open amber/red event, record the actions actually executed with their dates and the realised ratio uplift.
Compare the realised uplift to the estimate on the action menu and record the variance.
Only move the event to closed once two consecutive monthly readings sit above the trigger level.
Where the ratio did not recover, escalate again rather than extending the remediation date a second time.
checklist.done: each trigger event closes on two consecutive readings above the trigger with realised-versus-estimated uplift recorded.

checklist.step: File the monitoring evidence for retention
actions: Move each month's capital pack, reserve worksheet, trigger register extract and escalation correspondence into the repository under Japan / Solvency / <business year>.
Apply the 10-year retention label so the records survive the FSA inspection cycle.
Index each record by business year, month, ratio value and trigger status so an inspector's question can be answered without a rebuild.
Confirm the index returns all 12 months before the business year is signed off.
checklist.done: all 12 monthly packs plus both accrual worksheets are filed, labelled for 10 years and retrievable by month and ratio.

testing.step: Build the population of monitoring cycles and trigger events
actions: Extract from the capital trigger register every monthly row for the period under test plus every event raised.
Compare the row count to the number of month ends in the period — a missing month is an exception before any sampling happens.
Add the 30 September and 31 March Art. 115 accrual worksheets to the population.
Sign the population extract as complete and date it.
testing.done: the population covers every month end and both statutory accruals, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the monitored reserve balances to the statutory ledger
actions: Pull the price fluctuation reserve, contingency reserve and policy reserve closing balances from the GL at the interim and year end.
Agree each to the corresponding figure in the monitoring pack and to the Appointed Actuary's valuation summary.
Investigate any difference above JPY 1 million and record the explanation and its source.
Treat an unexplained difference as an exception rather than a rounding note.
testing.done: all three reserve balances agree across ledger, monitoring pack and actuarial summary, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of monitoring cycles
actions: Take 100% of months carrying an amber or red trigger score.
Take 4 further months selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining green months.
Record population size, seed, selection date and sample size in the workpaper so the draw is reproducible.
Include both statutory accrual worksheets in the sample regardless of the draw.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers every triggered month and both accrual worksheets.

testing.step: Re-perform the price fluctuation reserve accrual independently
actions: Take the covered-asset base for the sampled period and independently apply the accumulation rates from the current Ordinance for Enforcement text — do not copy the company's rate cells.
Recompute the ceiling test per category and the resulting capped accrual.
Compare to the booked journal in SAP S/4HANA and record the difference in yen.
Any difference above JPY 1 million, or any rate that does not match the ordinance, is an exception.
testing.done: the recomputed accrual agrees to the booked entry within JPY 1 million with ordinance rates independently sourced.

testing.step: Re-perform the solvency margin ratio for two sampled months
actions: Re-run the solvency margin model for two sampled month ends from the archived input files using the recorded model run id.
Rebuild the numerator inclusions independently, especially the unrealised gain inclusion rate and the subordinated debt limit.
Recompute the risk correlation combination and the 0.5 factor in the denominator.
Compare to the reported SMR; a difference above 1.0 percentage point is an exception requiring a written explanation.
testing.done: both re-performed SMR figures land within 1.0 percentage point of the reported ratio.

testing.step: Test that the drawdown rule was respected
actions: List every debit to the price fluctuation reserve account in the period.
For each, pull the realised gain/loss detail on covered assets and recompute the net loss against the prescribed threshold.
Confirm the drawdown never exceeded the excess above the threshold and carried written CFO approval dated before the posting.
A drawdown taken to smooth earnings rather than to offset a threshold-breaching realised loss is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every reserve debit is supported by a recomputed threshold breach and a pre-dated CFO approval.

testing.step: Trace trigger escalations to timestamped evidence
actions: For each amber/red event, pull the ratio production timestamp from the model run log and the escalation notification timestamp from the mailbox.
Compute the elapsed business days between them and compare to the one-business-day standard.
Confirm the notification actually reached the CFO, CEO and Risk Committee Chair and named the ratio, driver and distance to the next threshold.
Trace any sub-250% event to the out-of-cycle Risk Committee minute.
testing.done: every triggered event shows escalation within one business day to all three named recipients, evidenced by timestamps.

testing.step: Recompute the distance-to-threshold and improvement plan clock
actions: For each sampled month recompute the headroom in percentage points from the reported SMR to the 200% Category 1 line and to the 100% Category 2 line.
Compare to the headroom quoted in the Board pack and flag any overstatement.
Where the ratio fell below 200%, count the business days from detection to the dated improvement plan draft and test it against the 5-business-day standard.
Confirm the plan's projected quarterly ratio path used the Appointed Actuary's confirmed reserve assumptions.
testing.done: reported headroom recomputes correctly and any sub-200% reading produced a plan inside 5 business days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the month, the control that failed and the yen or percentage-point impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: stale ordinance rate, asset base mis-mapping, model input error, late escalation, unapproved drawdown.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any unapproved drawdown or unescalated sub-200% reading.
Carry every open issue into the next test cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception carries an issue, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the population and compare to the zero-tolerance thresholds for skipped cycles and late escalations.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who prepared no monitoring pack in the period, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open breach to the Audit Committee and the Risk Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states an exception rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting dates.

checklist.step: Open the filing pack and confirm the prescribed forms are the current edition
actions: Create the filing workspace named JP-BusinessReport-<business year>-<annual|interim> and set the statutory due date to 30 June or 31 December.
Download the current prescribed Business Report forms and supplementary schedules from the FSA site and compare the form version stamp to last period's pack.
List every changed line item, added schedule or renumbered column and raise a change note for the affected schedule owner.
Attach the current Ordinance for Enforcement extract that prescribes the forms as the version evidence.
checklist.done: the workspace holds the current-edition forms with every change from the prior period noted and assigned.

checklist.step: Assign each schedule to a named owner with a due date
actions: Build the schedule ownership map: balance sheet and P&L to the Controller, policy reserve and outstanding claims schedules to the Valuation Actuary, price fluctuation and contingency reserve schedules to Capital Management, solvency margin schedule to the Capital Model Actuary, investment schedules to Investment Operations.
Set each owner's internal due date at T-20 from the statutory date so the tie-out has room.
Circulate the map with the change notes from the form comparison and get an acknowledgement per owner.
Track acknowledgement and draft status daily from T-45.
checklist.done: every prescribed schedule has a named owner, an internal T-20 due date and an acknowledgement on record.

checklist.step: Lock the statutory close and freeze the source figures
actions: Complete the statutory close for the period and set the ledger period status to closed so no post-filing journals can move the numbers.
Publish the frozen trial balance with a version id and timestamp to the filing workspace.
Confirm the price fluctuation reserve accrual, contingency reserve and policy reserve journals are all posted before the freeze.
Notify all schedule owners that the frozen trial balance is the only permitted source.
checklist.done: the ledger is closed, the frozen trial balance is published with a version id, and owners are notified.

checklist.step: Populate the reserve schedules from the actuarial valuation
actions: Export the Art. 116 policy reserve by product group, valuation method and valuation interest rate, and the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve split reported/IBNR.

Show separately the standard policy reserve blocks valued on the FSA-notified standard valuation interest rate and standard mortality table, and the non-standard blocks with the basic-document method used.
Enter the figures into the prescribed reserve schedules and reconcile the totals to the frozen trial balance liability accounts.
Attach the valuation summary and model run id behind each schedule cell block.
checklist.done: the reserve schedules are populated, split standard versus non-standard, and tie to the frozen trial balance.

checklist.step: Populate the price fluctuation reserve and solvency schedules
actions: Enter the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve roll-forward: opening balance, accrual at the ordinance rate per covered category, any threshold-tested drawdown, closing balance and headroom to the ceiling.
Enter the solvency margin schedule numerator and denominator components from the signed month-13 model run and state the ratio to one decimal place.
Cross-check that the price fluctuation reserve figure used in the solvency numerator equals the balance sheet figure to the yen.
Hand the completed schedules to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst with the supporting worksheets.
checklist.done: the reserve roll-forward and solvency schedule are complete and the reserve figure agrees across both.

checklist.step: Run the cross-schedule tie-out
actions: Build the tie-out workbook with one row per prescribed line item, its source (ledger account, actuarial summary, model output) and the two values being compared.

Test every internal cross-foot the forms require: total assets to total liabilities plus net assets, premium income to the segment schedule, reserve movement to the P&L charge, prior-year comparatives to last period's filed report.
Clear every difference above JPY 1 million with the schedule owner and record the explanation on the row.
Freeze the workbook and mark it the tie-out of record for the filing.
checklist.done: every prescribed line item ties to a named source with no unexplained difference above JPY 1 million.

checklist.step: Attach the Appointed Actuary's opinion
actions: Confirm the policy reserve in the filing is the reserve the opinion covers, at the same valuation date and on the same basis.
Perform the future cash-flow adequacy check on the in-force block and record the conclusion in the opinion.
Sign the opinion, state any qualification in plain terms, and submit it to the Board for receipt before the filing is transmitted.
Give the signed opinion to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for attachment to the filing pack.
checklist.done: a signed actuarial opinion covering the filed reserve is attached and has been received by the Board.

checklist.step: Put the pack through two-person review
actions: Review every schedule against the tie-out workbook and initial each schedule as reviewed.
Re-read the prescribed form instructions for units, rounding convention and negative-number presentation and correct anything that deviates.
Check the prior-period comparatives against the report as actually filed last period, not against a restated internal figure.
Reject the pack back to the owner where a schedule carries an unexplained tie-out difference rather than accepting a note.
checklist.done: every schedule carries a reviewer initial and the form instructions on units and rounding are satisfied.

checklist.step: Obtain the internal approvals recorded on the filing
actions: Review the filing summary: headline financials, solvency margin ratio, reserve balances and any actuarial qualification.
Approve the pack for submission in writing, naming the business year and the filing type.
Where the Appointed Actuary qualified the opinion, require the covering explanation to be drafted before approval.
Pass the approved pack to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for transmission.
checklist.done: a written CFO approval naming the period and filing type is on the pack before transmission.

checklist.step: Transmit the filing to the FSA and capture the receipt
actions: Log in to the FSA electronic application and notification system with the company's registered account and select the business report submission for the Japan entity.
Upload the prescribed forms, supplementary schedules and the signed actuarial opinion in the order the system requires, checking each attachment opens after upload.
Submit before the statutory due date — 30 June for the annual report, 31 December for the interim — and never on the due date itself.
Download the acknowledgement, record the acknowledgement number and submission timestamp on the filing workspace row, and file the receipt PDF.
checklist.done: the filing is transmitted before the statutory date with the acknowledgement number and receipt PDF on file.

checklist.step: Produce and publish the Art. 111 explanatory documents
actions: Build the explanatory document for public inspection from the filed figures — business overview, financial position, solvency margin ratio, reserve balances and the price fluctuation reserve.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the narrative sections for statements that go beyond the filed numbers.
Place the document for public inspection at the head office and branch offices and publish the electronic version on the corporate site without delay after the year end.
Record the publication date and the office locations where the paper copy is available.
checklist.done: the explanatory document is published electronically and available at the offices, with the date recorded.

checklist.step: Handle FSA follow-up questions on the filing
actions: Log every FSA or Local Finance Bureau query against the filing with the date received, the schedule and line item questioned and the response due date.
Draft the response with the schedule owner, attaching the tie-out row and source extract that supports the figure.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any response that concedes an error before it is sent.
Record the sent date and the regulator's closure of the query on the tracker row.
checklist.done: every regulator query has a logged response, a counsel clearance where needed, and a recorded closure.

checklist.step: Correct and resubmit where an error is found after filing
actions: On discovering a misstatement, quantify the effect on each affected schedule and on the solvency margin ratio.
Decide with the CFO and Regulatory Counsel whether the error requires an amended report or a written explanation, and record the reasoning.

Where an amended report is required, rebuild the affected schedules from the frozen trial balance, re-run the tie-out and resubmit through the FSA system with a covering note stating what changed and why.
Log the resubmission on the filing tracker with both acknowledgement numbers.
checklist.done: any post-filing error has a quantified impact, a documented decision and, where needed, a resubmission with both acknowledgement numbers.

checklist.step: Run the post-filing lessons review before the next cycle
actions: Within 10 business days of submission, review every late schedule, every tie-out difference and every reviewer rejection from the cycle.
Assign each to a cause — form change missed, source not frozen, owner unclear, actuarial input late — and agree an action with the owner.
Update the schedule ownership map and the internal due dates for the next cycle from those actions.
Circulate the revised map with the next cycle's kick-off.
checklist.done: the cycle review is complete within 10 business days with actions folded into the next cycle's ownership map.

checklist.step: Retain the full filing record
actions: File the submitted forms, schedules, tie-out workbook, actuarial opinion, CFO approval and FSA receipt as one indexed record per filing.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by business year, filing type and acknowledgement number.
Confirm the record can be retrieved by acknowledgement number in a single search.
Link the record to the Art. 111 explanatory document and its publication date.
checklist.done: one indexed, 10-year-labelled record per filing is retrievable by acknowledgement number and linked to the public document.

testing.step: Build the population of filings and schedules
actions: Extract every filing workspace row for the period: annual report, interim report, resubmissions and the Art. 111 document.
List the prescribed schedules the current forms require and confirm each appears in each filing — a missing schedule is an exception before sampling.
Reconcile the workspace list to the FSA acknowledgements actually received.
Sign and date the population extract.
testing.done: the population lists every filing and every prescribed schedule, reconciled to the acknowledgements received.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed figures back to the closed ledger
actions: Pull the frozen trial balance version referenced by the tie-out workbook and confirm the ledger period is still closed.
Agree total assets, total liabilities, net assets, premium income and the three reserve balances from the filed report to that trial balance.
Confirm no journal was posted to the period after the freeze timestamp; a post-freeze journal invalidates the tie-out.
Record every difference in yen with its explanation.
testing.done: filed headline figures agree to the frozen trial balance and no post-freeze journal exists.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of schedules
actions: Take 100% of the reserve schedules (Art. 115, 116, 117) and the solvency margin schedule.
Take 8 further schedules at random with a recorded seed from the remaining prescribed schedules.
Record population size, seed and selection date in the workpaper.
Cover both the annual and interim filings in the draw.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all reserve and solvency schedules and both filings.

testing.step: Re-perform the tie-out on the sampled schedules
actions: For each sampled schedule, independently trace each line item to its named source — ledger account, actuarial valuation summary or model output.
Re-run the internal cross-foots the forms require rather than accepting the company's tie-out row.
Check units, rounding and negative-number presentation against the prescribed form instructions.
Log any difference above JPY 1 million or any presentation deviation as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled schedule is independently traced and cross-footed with differences logged.

testing.step: Verify the prior-period comparatives against what was actually filed
actions: Retrieve the prior period's submitted report by acknowledgement number.
Compare every comparative column in the current filing to the prior filed figures line by line.
Where a comparative was restated, confirm the restatement is disclosed and the reason recorded.
An undisclosed restated comparative is an exception.
testing.done: all comparatives agree to the prior filed report or the restatement is disclosed and explained.

testing.step: Trace the actuarial opinion to the reserve actually filed
actions: Open the signed Appointed Actuary opinion attached to the filing and read the valuation date, the block covered and any qualification.
Agree the reserve amount in the opinion to the Art. 116 schedule in the filing to the yen.
Confirm the opinion was signed and received by the Board before the transmission timestamp.
An opinion dated after transmission, or covering a different valuation date, is an exception.
testing.done: the opinion covers the filed reserve at the filed valuation date and pre-dates transmission.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory deadline maths for each filing
actions: Recompute the annual due date as 3 months from the 31 March business-year end and the interim due date as 3 months from the 30 September half-year end.
Compare the FSA acknowledgement timestamp to the recomputed due date and record the days of margin or the days late.
Test the Art. 111 explanatory document publication date against the 'without delay after the year end' standard and record the elapsed days.
Any filing on or after the due date is treated as a fail regardless of acceptance by the system.
testing.done: each filing shows a recomputed due date and a measured margin, with any late filing flagged.

testing.step: Confirm the receipt evidence is complete and retrievable
actions: Search the repository by each acknowledgement number and confirm the search returns the full record in one hit.
Open the record and verify it holds the submitted PDFs, tie-out workbook, actuarial opinion, CFO approval and the FSA receipt.
Check the 10-year retention label is applied and the record is not editable.
Missing components or an unlabelled record is an exception.
testing.done: every filing record is retrievable by acknowledgement number, complete and labelled for 10-year retention.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the filing, the schedule, the difference in yen and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: stale form edition, unfrozen source, late actuarial input, comparative not traced, late transmission.
Name an owner and a remediation date; for a late filing or a resubmission, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry each open issue into the next filing cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the schedule exception rate and compare it to the zero-tolerance thresholds for late filing and missing opinion.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who owned no schedule in the filing under test, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Refresh the risk profile that the ORSA has to assess
actions: Export the risk register as at 31 March and re-score each risk with the business owner on likelihood and impact against the current in-force book.

Add or retire risks from the year's events: variable annuity minimum guarantee exposure, JGB reinvestment risk, equity concentration in the price-variable portfolio, mass lapse, operational and cyber events.
Map every material risk to a quantified capital charge or to an explicit statement of why it is not capitalised.
Circulate the refreshed profile to the Risk Committee for challenge before assumptions are locked.
checklist.done: every material risk is re-scored, owned and either capitalised or explicitly explained as uncapitalised.

checklist.step: Recalibrate the risk appetite statement and its limits
actions: Restate the appetite in measurable terms: minimum ESR, minimum solvency margin ratio, maximum equity exposure as a share of the general account, maximum duration mismatch in years.
Set the early-warning level above each hard limit and name the escalation body for each.
Have the Board approve any change to a limit before the projections are run against it.
Record the approved limit set with its effective date as the yardstick for this ORSA cycle.
checklist.done: an approved, measurable limit set with early-warning levels and named escalation bodies is in force for the cycle.

checklist.step: Lock the projection assumptions with the business plan
actions: Take the Board-approved 3-to-5-year business plan from Finance: new business volumes by product, expense plan, dividend plan and the investment strategy.
Set the economic assumptions: JPY yield curve, equity return, yen exchange rates, and the FSA-prescribed ultimate forward rate and last liquid point for the ESR basis.
Set the actuarial assumptions: mortality, lapse, and the standard valuation interest rate applying to new standard-reserve business.
Freeze the assumption pack by 31 May with sign-off from the Appointed Actuary, the Chief Investment Officer and the CFO.
checklist.done: a frozen, tri-signed assumption pack ties to the Board-approved business plan and the ESR basis.

checklist.step: Project capital and solvency over the plan horizon
actions: Run the base-case projection of the balance sheet, statutory solvency margin ratio and ESR for each year of the plan horizon.
Project the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve balance under the planned asset mix, showing accrual, ceiling headroom and any modelled drawdown.
Project the Art. 116 contingency reserve and policy reserve movement, separating standard-reserve and non-standard blocks.
Archive the run with the model version, assumption pack id and input hash in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: a base-case projection of SMR, ESR and all three reserves exists for every plan year with an archived, reproducible run.

checklist.step: Test the reserve buffers against the adverse cases
actions: Re-run the projection under the adverse cases agreed with the Risk Committee, including a sustained equity fall and a parallel JGB yield shock.
For each case compute the valuation loss on Art. 115 covered assets and compare it to the projected reserve balance to show whether the reserve absorbs it.
Compute the point in the projection at which a drawdown would exceed the prescribed threshold and become permissible, and state it in years.
Record whether the ESR and SMR stay above the appetite limits in every case and by how many percentage points.
checklist.done: each adverse case states the reserve absorption, the drawdown trigger point and the headroom against appetite limits.

checklist.step: Get the model independently validated before the report is drafted
actions: Review the capital model against the model risk policy: conceptual soundness, assumption support, code change control and back-testing of last year's projection against actuals.
Re-perform two projection years independently from the archived inputs and compare to the reported figures.
Raise validation findings with severity, owner and due date; a critical finding blocks the ORSA from proceeding.
Issue the validation report and file it with the model run archive.
checklist.done: a dated validation report exists with no open critical finding and two independently re-performed projection years.

checklist.step: Write the ORSA report to the structure the supervisor expects
actions: Draft the report in sections: risk management framework and governance, risk profile, risk appetite and limits, capital adequacy assessment on both the statutory and economic bases, stress and scenario results, and the conclusion on capital sufficiency over the horizon.
State plainly whether current and projected capital is sufficient, and where it is not, name the management actions and their dates.
Reference each figure to its model run id and assumption pack so nothing in the narrative is unsourced.
Circulate the draft to the CFO, Appointed Actuary and Chief Investment Officer for factual challenge before it goes to committee.
checklist.done: a complete draft covering all six sections exists with every figure referenced to a model run and challenged by the three executives.

checklist.step: Take the ORSA through the Risk Committee
actions: Table the draft ORSA, the validation report and the adverse-case results at the Risk Committee by 30 June.
Walk the committee through the appetite breaches shown by the projection and the proposed management actions.
Capture every committee challenge and the response in the minutes, and update the report where the challenge changes a conclusion.
Obtain the committee's recommendation to the Board.
checklist.done: the Risk Committee has minuted its challenge and recommended the ORSA to the Board.

checklist.step: Obtain the Board resolution on the ORSA
actions: Publish the final ORSA, the validation report and the Risk Committee minute to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting.
Put a resolution to the Board approving the ORSA report and the conclusion on capital sufficiency.
Ensure the minute names the report version, the date, and any condition the Board attached to its approval.
Return any conditional approval to the Enterprise Risk Manager with the condition and its due date.
checklist.done: a Board minute records approval of the named ORSA version and any condition with a due date.

checklist.step: Submit the ORSA report to the FSA
actions: Assemble the submission set: Board-approved ORSA report, the resolution extract and any appendix the supervisor requested at the last dialogue.
Transmit through the FSA electronic application and notification system to the Insurance Business Division in line with the supervisory schedule.
Capture the acknowledgement number and timestamp and record them on the ORSA workspace row.
File the receipt with the report in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: the Board-approved report is transmitted with the acknowledgement number and receipt on file.

checklist.step: Prove the ORSA was used, not just written
actions: Name the decisions taken in the year that cite the ORSA: investment strategy limits, product pricing changes, reinsurance of the minimum guarantee block, dividend decisions.
For each decision, point to the meeting minute that references the ORSA conclusion.
Where a plan assumption was changed because of the ORSA, record the before and after values.
Include the use-test evidence as an appendix to the next cycle's report.
checklist.done: at least three named decisions in the year trace to an ORSA conclusion through a dated minute.

checklist.step: Monitor the appetite limits between cycles
actions: Load the approved limits into the limit monitoring dashboard with their early-warning levels.
Refresh actuals monthly from the capital monitoring pack and the investment position file.
Raise a limit event the same day an early-warning level is passed, naming the escalation body from the appetite statement.
Report limit status to the Risk Committee each quarter with the trend since the ORSA.
checklist.done: every approved limit is monitored monthly with same-day events on early-warning breaches and quarterly committee reporting.

checklist.step: Trigger an out-of-cycle ORSA on a material change
actions: Define the triggers in the procedure: a hard-limit breach, a major acquisition or block reinsurance, a market move that cuts ESR by more than 20 percentage points, or a change in the FSA solvency framework.
On a trigger, decide within 10 business days whether a full or targeted re-run is needed and record the decision and reasoning.
Run the targeted projection on refreshed data and take the conclusion back to the Risk Committee.
Notify the FSA where the re-run changes the conclusion on capital sufficiency.
checklist.done: each trigger has a recorded decision inside 10 business days and, where re-run, a committee-reviewed conclusion.

checklist.step: Close out the validation findings and Board conditions
actions: Track every open validation finding and Board condition on a single action log with owner and due date.
Require evidence of the fix — a model change record, a rerun, or an updated assumption sign-off — before closing an item.
Report ageing items to the Risk Committee each quarter.
Carry anything still open into the next ORSA cycle as a stated limitation in the report.
checklist.done: every finding and condition is closed with evidence or carried into the next report as a stated limitation.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle evidence
actions: File the ORSA report, assumption pack, model run archive reference, validation report, committee and Board minutes and the FSA receipt as one indexed cycle record.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by business year and report version.
Confirm each referenced model run is still retrievable from the model governance repository.
Link the use-test evidence to the same cycle record.
checklist.done: one indexed cycle record holds every ORSA artefact, is labelled for 10 years, and its model runs still resolve.

testing.step: Build the population of ORSA artefacts for the cycle
actions: List the cycle's artefacts: report versions, assumption pack, model runs, validation report, committee papers, Board minute and FSA receipt.
Check each required artefact exists and is dated; a missing validation report or Board minute is an exception before sampling.
Add any out-of-cycle ORSA and its trigger record to the population.
Sign and date the population extract.
testing.done: the population lists every required artefact for the cycle, each present and dated.

testing.step: Reconcile the ORSA opening balance sheet to the filed statutory position
actions: Agree the ORSA's opening total assets, policy reserve, contingency reserve and price fluctuation reserve to the 31 March business report as filed.
Agree the opening solvency margin ratio to the filed solvency schedule to one decimal place.
Investigate any difference and record whether it comes from a legitimate economic-basis adjustment or an error.
An unexplained difference in the opening position invalidates the projection and is an exception.
testing.done: the ORSA opening position agrees to the filed statutory report or every difference is explained as a basis adjustment.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of projections and assumptions
actions: Take 100% of the adverse cases and the base case's final projection year.
Take 6 assumptions at random with a recorded seed from the frozen assumption pack.
Record population size, seed and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Include every risk shown as breaching an appetite limit in the projection.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all adverse cases plus every projected limit breach.

testing.step: Re-perform two projection years in the model
actions: Restore the archived run by model version and input hash and re-run the base case for two plan years.
Rebuild the ESR own-funds and required-capital components independently rather than reading the model summary.
Compare the re-performed SMR and ESR to the reported figures for those years.
A difference above 1.0 percentage point, or a run that cannot be restored from the archive, is an exception.
testing.done: two projection years reproduce from the archive within 1.0 percentage point on both ratios.

testing.step: Trace sampled assumptions to their approved source
actions: For each sampled assumption, find its source: the Board-approved business plan, the investment strategy paper, the actuarial experience study, or the FSA-prescribed ESR basis.
Confirm the value used in the model equals the source value and the sign-off pre-dates the assumption freeze date of 31 May.
Where the assumption differs from experience, confirm the deviation is explained in the assumption pack.
An assumption without a traceable, pre-dated source is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled assumption traces to an approved source signed before the freeze date.

testing.step: Recompute the reserve buffer adequacy in the adverse cases
actions: For each adverse case, independently recompute the modelled valuation loss on Art. 115 covered assets from the shocked market values.
Compare the loss to the projected price fluctuation reserve balance and reproduce the stated absorption percentage.
Recompute the year in which a permissible drawdown would first arise using the prescribed threshold.
Any restatement of absorption or drawdown timing is an exception with the corrected figure recorded.
testing.done: reserve absorption and drawdown timing reproduce independently for every adverse case.

testing.step: Trace the governance chain from draft to submission
actions: Match the report version number in the Board minute to the version transmitted to the FSA.
Confirm the papers were published at least 5 business days before the Board meeting.
Read the Risk Committee minute for the recorded challenge and confirm any change it demanded appears in the final version.
A submitted version that differs from the resolved version is a reportable governance breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: the submitted version equals the Board-resolved version and committee challenges are reflected in it.

testing.step: Test the use of the ORSA in actual decisions
actions: Take the decisions the CEO cited as ORSA-driven and open the minute for each.
Confirm the minute genuinely references the ORSA conclusion rather than mentioning risk generically.
Where a plan assumption changed, agree the before and after values to the plan documents.
Fewer than three traceable decisions is an exception against the use-test expectation.
testing.done: at least three decisions trace to an ORSA conclusion through a dated minute with values agreed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the artefact, the failure and its effect on the capital sufficiency conclusion.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: assumption unsourced, run not reproducible, open critical validation finding, governance sequence broken, use-test not evidenced.
Name an owner and a remediation date, and escalate any issue that changes the capital sufficiency conclusion to the CRO the same day.
Carry every open issue into the next ORSA cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate across artefacts and compare to the zero-tolerance thresholds for a missing Board resolution or an open critical validation finding.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, independent of the capital modelling team, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Risk Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting dates.

checklist.step: Refresh and approve the scenario library for the cycle
actions: Open the scenario library and review each scenario against the current risk profile — drop only what the Risk Committee approves in writing.

Cover the mandatory families: equity shock, JGB yield shift up and down, credit spread widening, yen appreciation, mass lapse, pandemic mortality, and a Nankai Trough-scale earthquake affecting operations and assets.
Add a combined adverse scenario that runs equity, rates and lapse together rather than in isolation.
Take the library to the Risk Committee for approval by 30 April and record the approval date against each scenario.
checklist.done: every scenario in the library carries a Risk Committee approval date and the mandatory families are all represented.

checklist.step: Calibrate each shock from a named external source
actions: For the equity shock, pull the TOPIX and Nikkei 225 drawdown history and set the shock at a stated percentile with the observation window recorded.
For the rate shocks, pull the JGB par curve history and set the parallel and steepening shifts in basis points per tenor.
For the FX shock, pull the USD/JPY and EUR/JPY history and set the yen appreciation percentage.
Record for every calibration the source, the data window, the percentile and the date pulled — a shock with no source is not approved.
Send the calibration pack to the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary for review.
checklist.done: every market shock has a named source, data window and percentile recorded in the calibration pack.

checklist.step: Cut and reconcile the input data at the valuation date
actions: Export the 31 March general account position file with book value, market value, duration and credit rating per holding.
Tag every holding to its Art. 115 covered category so the reserve absorption test can be run on the right base.
Reconcile market values to the closed statutory ledger and clear differences above JPY 1 million with the Controller.
Publish the reconciled data cut with a version id to the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the position file is Art. 115-tagged, reconciled to the ledger and published with a version id.

checklist.step: Set the liability response assumptions for each scenario
actions: Specify how policyholder behaviour moves under each scenario — dynamic lapse under a rate rise, surrender under an equity fall on variable annuity contracts.
Specify the reserve response: whether the Art. 116 policy reserve strengthens under the scenario and whether the contingency reserve can be drawn.
State the variable annuity minimum guarantee cost response under the equity and rate shocks separately.
Sign the liability assumption set and file it with the calibration pack.
checklist.done: each scenario has a signed liability response covering behaviour, reserves and minimum guarantee cost.

checklist.step: Run the single-factor shocks
actions: Load the reconciled data cut and the approved calibrations, and run each single-factor scenario against the 31 March balance sheet.
Produce for each: post-shock own funds, post-shock solvency margin ratio, post-shock ESR, and the change in each in percentage points.
Confirm the model applied the shock to every affected asset class — spot-check a domestic equity, a foreign bond and a derivative position by hand.
Archive each run with model version, calibration id and input hash.
checklist.done: every single-factor scenario has an archived, reproducible run reporting post-shock SMR and ESR.

checklist.step: Run the combined adverse and reverse stress tests
actions: Run the combined adverse scenario applying equity, rate, credit and lapse shocks simultaneously with the agreed correlation treatment.
Run the reverse stress test: solve for the combination of shocks that drives ESR to 100% and SMR to 200%, and state the shock magnitudes that get there.
Describe in words the business situation the reverse stress represents so the Board can judge plausibility.
Archive both runs alongside the single-factor set.
checklist.done: the combined scenario and a solved reverse stress test are archived with the shock magnitudes that breach each threshold stated.

checklist.step: Test whether the price fluctuation reserve absorbs the modelled loss
actions: For each market scenario, compute the valuation loss on Art. 115 covered assets by category from the shocked market values.
Compare the loss to the opening reserve balance per category and express absorption as a percentage of the loss covered.
Compute the realised loss level at which the prescribed drawdown threshold would be crossed and whether the scenario crosses it.
Show the residual loss that would fall to capital after the reserve is exhausted.
checklist.done: each scenario reports covered-asset loss, reserve absorption percentage, drawdown threshold status and residual loss to capital.

checklist.step: Compare results to the risk appetite limits
actions: Score each scenario's post-shock ESR and SMR against the approved appetite limits and early-warning levels.
List every scenario that breaches a limit with the breach size in percentage points.
Rank scenarios by severity so the Board sees the binding constraint rather than the full grid.
Take the ranked list into the challenge session.
checklist.done: every scenario is scored against appetite with breaches sized and the scenario grid ranked by severity.

checklist.step: Hold a results challenge session with the first line
actions: Walk the investment, product and ALM leads through the ranked results and the drivers behind each.
Challenge any result that looks counter-intuitive — an equity shock that barely moves ESR usually means a hedge is double-counted.
Record each challenge, the response and any re-run agreed, with an owner and a date.
Sign the results pack as challenged before it is used anywhere else.
checklist.done: the results pack carries a minuted challenge with owners for every agreed re-run.

checklist.step: Attach credible management actions to the severe scenarios
actions: For every scenario breaching an appetite limit, name the management actions that would be taken and the ratio uplift each delivers.
State the lead time and the approval body for each action and confirm it is executable in the scenario's own market conditions.
Strike out any action that depends on markets that would be closed in the scenario — a subordinated debt issue in a credit crisis is not credible.
Show post-action ratios separately from pre-action ratios so the Board sees both.
checklist.done: each limit-breaching scenario carries credible, lead-timed actions with pre- and post-action ratios shown separately.

checklist.step: Get the results independently validated
actions: Check every approved scenario has a run and that no run used an unapproved calibration.
Independently re-run two scenarios from the archived inputs and compare the post-shock ratios.
Review whether the shock actually propagated to the liability side rather than only to assets.
Issue findings with severity and owner; a critical finding blocks the results from feeding the ORSA.
checklist.done: a dated validation report confirms library completeness, two reproduced runs and no open critical finding.

checklist.step: Report the results to the Board with the reserve position
actions: Publish the results pack with the ranked scenarios, the reverse stress conclusion, the Art. 115 reserve absorption table and the management action menu.
Put the stress testing conclusion to the Board alongside the ORSA at the July meeting.
Record in the minute the scenarios that breached appetite and the actions the Board endorsed.
Return any Board-requested additional scenario to the Capital Model Actuary with a due date.
checklist.done: the Board minute records the stress results, the appetite breaches and the endorsed actions.

checklist.step: Feed the results into the ORSA and the investment strategy
actions: Hand the finalised scenario results to the ORSA drafting team before the assumption freeze so the report uses this cycle's numbers.
Give the Chief Investment Officer the scenarios that breached appetite so the strategic asset allocation review can respond.
Where the results support a limit change, route the proposal through the Risk Committee rather than adjusting the limit informally.
Record where each result was used.
checklist.done: the results are recorded as used in the ORSA, the asset allocation review and any limit proposal.

checklist.step: Re-run out of cycle when the world moves
actions: Monitor the triggers: a TOPIX fall beyond the calibrated shock, a JGB yield move beyond the calibrated shift, a block acquisition, or a change in the FSA field-test specification.
On a trigger, re-run the affected scenarios on refreshed data within 10 business days.
Report the re-run results to the Risk Committee with a comparison to the annual run.
Log the trigger, the decision and the run reference.
checklist.done: every trigger has a logged decision and, where re-run, results compared to the annual run at the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle's testing evidence
actions: File the approved scenario library, calibration pack, data cut version, run archive references, results pack, challenge minute, validation report and Board minute as one cycle record.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by business year and scenario name.
Confirm each archived run reference still resolves in the model governance repository.
Check the record can be retrieved by scenario name in a single search.
checklist.done: one indexed cycle record holds every artefact, is labelled for 10 years, and every run reference still resolves.

testing.step: Build the population of approved scenarios and runs
actions: Extract the Risk Committee-approved scenario library with approval dates.
Extract the run register from the model governance repository for the cycle.
Match them one to one; an approved scenario with no run, or a run with no approved scenario, is an exception before sampling.
Add the reverse stress test and any out-of-cycle run and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: every approved scenario matches exactly one archived run, with mismatches listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile the stress input data to the statutory position
actions: Agree the pre-shock total market value and book value in the data cut to the 31 March investment sub-ledger.
Agree the Art. 115 covered-asset base used in the absorption test to the reserve schedule filed in the business report.
Agree the opening policy reserve and contingency reserve to the actuarial valuation summary.
An unreconciled input base makes every downstream result an exception.
testing.done: all pre-shock balances agree to the ledger, the filed reserve schedule and the valuation summary.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of scenarios
actions: Take 100% of scenarios that breached an appetite limit, plus the combined adverse and reverse stress runs.
Take 4 further scenarios at random with a recorded seed from the remaining library.
Record population size, seed and selection date in the workpaper.
Include every scenario whose calibration changed from the prior cycle.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all breaching, combined, reverse and recalibrated scenarios.

testing.step: Trace each sampled calibration to its external source
actions: For each sampled market shock, pull the same index or curve history for the recorded data window.
Recompute the stated percentile and compare it to the calibrated shock magnitude.
Confirm the calibration date pre-dates the Risk Committee approval date for that scenario.
A shock that cannot be reproduced from its own stated source and window is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled shock reproduces from its stated source, window and percentile, and pre-dates its approval.

testing.step: Re-perform two scenario runs in the model
actions: Restore two sampled runs by model version and input hash and execute them again.
Compare post-shock own funds, SMR and ESR to the reported figures.
Check the shock reached the liability side by inspecting the minimum guarantee cost and lapse output, not only the asset values.
A difference above 1.0 percentage point or a run that will not restore is an exception.
testing.done: both re-performed runs reproduce within 1.0 percentage point with the liability response confirmed present.

testing.step: Recompute the Art. 115 reserve absorption arithmetic
actions: For each sampled scenario, independently compute the covered-asset valuation loss by category from the shocked market values.
Recompute absorption as reserve balance ÷ loss and compare to the reported percentage.
Recompute whether the prescribed drawdown threshold is crossed and compare to the reported status.
Recompute the residual loss falling to capital and reconcile it to the reported post-shock own funds movement.
testing.done: absorption percentage, drawdown status and residual loss all reproduce and tie to the reported own funds movement.

testing.step: Test the credibility of the assumed management actions
actions: For each limit-breaching scenario, take the assumed actions and check each has a named approval body and a stated lead time.
Challenge any action requiring a market that the scenario itself closes, and any action assuming a counterparty that the scenario stresses.
Agree the claimed ratio uplift to a supporting calculation rather than a management estimate.
An uplift with no calculation behind it is an exception.
testing.done: every assumed action has an approval body, a lead time, a supporting uplift calculation and survives the scenario's own conditions.

testing.step: Trace results into the ORSA and the Board minute
actions: Compare the scenario figures quoted in the ORSA report to the finalised results pack line by line.
Confirm the Board minute records the appetite breaches and the endorsed actions.
Confirm any Board-requested additional scenario was run and reported back with a date.
A figure that changed between the results pack and the ORSA without a documented reason is an exception.
testing.done: every scenario figure in the ORSA matches the results pack and the Board minute records the breaches and actions.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the scenario, the failure and its effect on the reported severity.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: calibration unsourced, scenario not run, run not reproducible, shock not propagated to liabilities, action not credible.
Name an owner and a remediation date; escalate to the CRO the same day where a corrected result would breach an appetite limit.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over the scenario population against the zero-tolerance thresholds for unrun scenarios and irreproducible runs.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who built and calibrated no scenario in the library, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Risk Committee and the Audit Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting dates.
